cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Structural systems support loads without failing; engineers must understand loads, forces and failure modes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Static (dead) loads are constant, permanent forces (e.g. the weight of the structure itself).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Dynamic (live) loads vary over time (e.g. wind, vehicles, occupants, machinery vibration).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Space frame structures use interconnected triangulated members for lightweight, rigid construction (e.g. crane jibs, roof structures).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Monocoque structures carry loads through the outer skin rather than an internal frame (e.g. car bodies, aircraft fuselages).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Bending occurs when a load causes a beam to curve; the outer surface is in tension, the inner surface is in compression.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Buckling is sudden lateral failure of a slender column under compressive load; it occurs before the material's compressive strength is reached.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Pneumatic systems use compressed air to transmit force and motion; used in automation, robotics and factory machinery.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Hydraulic systems use pressurised liquid (usually oil) to transmit force; they can generate very high forces (e.g. presses, excavators).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Pascal's Law: pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions; this is the principle behind hydraulic multiplication.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Pneumatic advantages: clean (air exhausts to atmosphere), fast, safe in hazardous environments. Disadvantages: lower force than hydraulics, compressible medium.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Structural & Pneumatic Systems
cards.back: Hydraulic advantages: very high forces, precise control, incompressible medium. Disadvantages: oil leaks are hazardous, slower than pneumatics.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — structural & pneumatic systems?
cards.back: 1. For Structural & Pneumatic Systems questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Structural & Pneumatic Systems through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
A factory needs a system to lift heavy steel plates (up to 5 tonnes). Compare pneumatic and hydraulic solutions, recommending the most suitable with justification. [6 marks]

AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of structural & pneumatic systems to analyse, design and manufacture engineering solutions. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate engineer
